observations: Observed screenshots: the large two-line desktop headline, compact navigation and rust CTA produce a deliberate editorial hierarchy. The framed wide film, ruled project list with separated years and large offset About statement form a coherent page rather than isolated components.

Observed screenshots: mobile retains a readable two-line headline and complete single-row navigation. The CTA, nearly square footage, work titles/years and About statement use consistent gutters without apparent horizontal clipping. The complete yellow subject remains inside the video and poster crops.

Observed views.json: both normal captures report active playback at approximately 1.7 seconds. Both reduced-motion captures report paused video at time zero and hidden video; actual screenshots preserve a static poster and all page content. All four captures report no errors.

Observed screenshots/source: the square pause control is visible during normal playback. Source inference: playback is governed by explicit user pause, viewport and tab visibility, reduced motion and asynchronous-attempt guards; playback rejection/error retains the poster and supplies status text. Manual pause replaces the current moving frame with the poster, creating a minor continuity jump. Footage supplies the primary motion, with restrained hover feedback.

Source inference: persisted pagehide pauses without discarding listeners, and persisted pageshow recomputes viewport visibility and synchronizes playback. This is a restoration path in code, not browser verification of restoration.

Source/brief assessment: required navigation, hero text, both project entries, About copy, local media, colors, system sans and square controls are present without fabricated claims, new destinations or added sections. No material authority/preservation failure was found.

Asset evidence: rights.json identifies locally authored repository-owned synthetic fixture media. The actual SHA-256 hashes of poster.svg and scene.webm match the manifest; source uses the corresponding local paths.
limitations: Reviewed rubric, exact brief, index.html, rights.json, views.json and all four actual screenshots. File hashes were independently checked; keyboard traversal, pause/retry, failure injection, live preference changes and lifecycle restoration were not independently exercised.

The desktop full-page images were scaled by the image viewer. No 768px or short-landscape capture was supplied. Static screenshots and sampled telemetry establish composition/playback state, not temporal smoothness or every failure path.

Observed control defect: both normal screenshots show a play triangle while their accompanying telemetry reports active playback. The visible control therefore communicates the wrong action/state to sighted users. Source inference: setPlaying assigns .hidden on SVG elements, which does not reliably reflect the HTML hidden attribute used by the CSS selector; the initially hidden pause SVG remains hidden. The button aria-label is separately updated correctly in source. The mismatch is observed; the specific browser-property cause was not independently reproduced.

Observed/source finish gap: the new media control appears substantially smaller than the primary action and is approximately 40 by 32 pixels in the 375px capture; source gives the media button no 44px minimum target. Existing CTA and details controls retain their supplied styling, so the small original details control is not treated as a preservation failure.

Source inference: modest 14px entrance/reveal animations leave ordinary content visible and avoid animating focusable controls or their containers. Reduced-motion changes cancel active animations. Playback includes explicit pause, visibility checks, asynchronous-attempt guards and a static poster after rejection/error. Manual pause swaps to the poster rather than freezing the current frame.

Source inference: pagehide permanently cleans up added motion and playback listeners/observers, leaving a static poster on back-forward-cache restoration. That is a robustness limitation outside supplied runtime coverage; the brief does not explicitly require added-media restoration. Original analytics and details listeners remain present.

Source/brief assessment: all original copy, IDs, destinations, two sections, theme tokens, CTA/control styles, analytics and details-toggle code are preserved. No fabricated marketing claims, extra destinations or sections were found.
